title: Take-up of July 2025 Child LifeSG Credits and whether their 12-month validity will be extended
asked: Mr David Hoe asked what share of the Child LifeSG Credits given out in July 2025 has not been used yet, and whether the Ministry would extend the 12-month validity period while stepping up outreach if take-up is lower than expected.
response: As of April 2026, 83% of the Child LifeSG Credits disbursed in July 2025 have been utilised. The Ministry has been sending reminders through social media, the LifeSG app and SMS, and will send a final reminder in June before the credits expire in July 2026; there will be no extension as there has been ample notice. On the supplementary questions, Mr Goh said the credits were designed for parents with young children, and pointed to Budget 2025's $500 credit for children above 12 (Edusave top-up for ages 13 to 16, Post-Secondary Education Account for ages 17 to 20). He also said this year's Budget announced a further tranche of $500 for all children in July, and that Large Family LifeSG Credits were disbursed last month.

key_points.point: 83% of the Child LifeSG Credits disbursed in July 2025 had been utilised as of April 2026
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: As of April 2026, 83% of the Child LifeSG Credits (CLC) disbursed in July 2025 have been utilised.

key_points.point: Reminders are issued via social media, the LifeSG app and SMS
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The Ministry has been issuing reminders to utilise the credits via our social media platforms, as well as via the LifeSG app and SMS messages.

key_points.point: A final reminder will go to recipients with unused credits in June, before the July 2026 expiry
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We will also send a final reminder to recipients with unused credits in June, before the credits expire in July 2026.

key_points.point: No extension of the validity period
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: As there has been ample notice, there will be no extension.

key_points.point: The credits were designed to support parents with young children on child-rearing costs
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: CLC was designed to support our parents with young children with child-rearing costs.

key_points.point: Budget 2025 provided a $500 credit for children above 12, with top-ups to Edusave for ages 13 to 16 and the Post-Secondary Education Account for ages 17 to 20
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: a $500 credit to children above 12 years old

key_points.point: Reasons given for unused credits include families still spreading out their spending, inertia, families being overseas, and some being unaware
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: In some cases, there is inertia.

key_points.point: A further tranche of $500 for all children will be disbursed this July
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: this July, there will be another tranche to all our children of $500

key_points.point: Large Family LifeSG Credits were disbursed to eligible families last month
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: last month, we have also disbursed the Large Family LifeSG Credits for eligible families.

left_open: Whether the Child LifeSG Credits themselves would be extended to children above 12, beyond the Budget 2025 Edusave and Post-Secondary Education Account top-ups.
supplementary: Reasons behind the unused credits and whether the credits could be extended to children older than 12.
